description: Conversion of loft space involving side and rear dormer extensions including the removal of a chimney stack. Alterations to the rear fenestration.
decision_conditions: The proposed side and rear dormer extension, by reason of its orientation, design, size, width, depth and the choice of flat roof form and uncharacteristic finish for extensions at roof level, would appear as a second floor extension, that is box-like and top-heavy on the side and rear elevation and would constitute an incongruous, unsympathetic and over dominant form of development that would not be subservient to the main building and would not be in-keeping with the prevailing pattern of development in the area. The proposal would not preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the dwelling, the terrace row of six properties, the wider streetscene and Carshalton Village Conservation Area, and is therefore contrary to Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and the advice in Supplementary Planning Document 4: Design of Residential Extensions (SPD4) and Supplementary Planning Document 14: Urban Design Guide - Creating Locally Distinctive Places (SPD14).

The proposed rear window at first floor, due to its slit-shaped vertical shape would form an incongruous addition to the dwelling that would adversely impact on the character and appearance of the main building and the terraced row of six dwellings, as seen from vintage points along Palmerston Road streetscene in Carshalton Village Conservation Area. As such, the first floor fenestration element is contrary to Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan and the guidance in Supplementary Planning Document 'Design of Residential Extensions' (SPD4) and Sutton's Urban Design Guide 'Creating Locally Distinctive Places' SPD (SPD14).
